q: What hinge has one leaf mortised into the door edge and the other surface-mounted on the frame?
n: A half-mortise hinge has one leaf mortised into the door edge and the other surface-mounted on the frame. A full-mortise hinge sets both leaves into mortises. Source: BHMA A156.1 (butts and hinges).

q: Which of these doors does NOT hang on hinges?
n: A sliding door moves on a track and rollers, so it needs no hinges. Accordion, bifold and swing doors all turn on hinges or pivots. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What hinge suits a door between kitchen and dining area that swings both ways?
n: A double-acting spring (or gravity) hinge lets a door swing both ways and return to center, ideal for kitchen–dining doors that servers push through either way. Source: BHMA A156.17 (double-acting hinges); Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (food service).

q: Which hinge runs the full length of the door and suits heavy, high-use doors?
n: A piano (continuous) hinge runs the full length of the door and spreads the load evenly. That suits heavy, high-traffic doors and prevents sagging. Source: BHMA A156.26 (continuous hinges).

q: Which hinge closes the door by its own built-in spring?
n: A spring hinge has a coiled spring in its barrel that swings the door shut by itself after it is released. Half-mortise, flap and drop-leaf hinges do not self-close. Source: BHMA A156.17 (self-closing hinges).

q: Which type of door can accommodate a large number of people at the same time and resists heavy winds?
n: A revolving door has three or four wings turning in a drum, so it moves a steady stream of people while always sealing the opening. That resists wind and stack-effect drafts in tall buildings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (entrances).

q: Which type of door provides a wide opening and offers a good vista for viewing?
n: Bi-fold doors fold and stack to one side, so almost the entire opening clears. That gives the widest unobstructed view of the vista. A sliding door always leaves at least one fixed panel in the opening, and French doors are limited to two hinged leaves. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8 (Folding and Bi-fold Doors); Time-Saver Standards for Housing (door types).

q: Which door is commonly used for wardrobes?
n: Bifold doors fold in half on a top track, so wardrobes open almost the full width with only a shallow swing. That makes them standard for closets. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; Time-Saver Standards (residential storage).

q: Which type of door is least effective at keeping heat outside and cold air inside?
n: An ordinary swing door opens a direct path for air each time it is used and has no vestibule effect. Revolving doors and sliding doors with air curtains limit air exchange. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (infiltration through doors).

q: Which type of door is commonly used in hospital operating rooms?
n: Operating rooms use wide double-leaf, double-swing (or automatic sliding hermetic) doors, so stretchers pass through and staff can push through with their shoulders without touching handles, keeping sterile hands. Source: DOH Planning and Design Guidelines for Hospitals; Time-Saver Standards (hospitals).

q: Which of these is a door leaf material?
n: Plywood is used as the face skins and leaves of flush and panel doors. Gypsum, fiber cement and hardboard are wall and ceiling boards, not door leaf materials. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (doors).

q: Where should you locate the door jamb for a toilet and bath?
o: Before the threshold outside the T&B
After the threshold inside the T&B
n: The jamb is set directly above the threshold, so the door closes against the stop at the line where the finish changes and the threshold or raised curb stops bathroom water from flowing out. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door frames and thresholds).

q: Which of the following is not a hardware component that supports a door?
n: The jamb is part of the door frame, not hardware. Pivot hinges, floor flanges and locksets are hardware items that hang, hold or secure the door. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; BHMA A156 hardware categories.

q: What is the structural member placed over a door or window opening?
n: A header (lintel) spans over a door or window opening and carries the wall or floor load above to the studs or masonry on each side. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which door type saves the most space?
n: A sliding door moves parallel to the wall and needs no swing clearance, so it saves the most floor space. Swing, pivot and revolving doors all sweep an arc. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which of these is a well-known lockset brand in the Philippines?
n: Schlage, part of Allegion, is a widely distributed lockset brand in the Philippines. Corona is a local hardware brand, Davies is paint and HCG is sanitary ware. Source: Schlage/Allegion company website; local hardware supplier catalogs.

q: Which local brand is known for manufacturing affordable door hinges and locksets in the Philippines?
n: Corona is a local brand of affordable hinges, locks and door hardware sold in Philippine hardware stores. Dorma, Yale and Hettich are foreign premium brands. Source: Local hardware supplier catalogs.

q: Which brand is widely used locally for high-security locksets and deadbolts?
n: Kwikset, a US brand, is widely sold locally for keyed locksets and deadbolts, including high-security SmartKey cylinders. Davies and Nippon are paint brands and Corona is budget hardware. Source: Kwikset company website.

q: Which brand is popular for door closers and floor hinges?
n: Dorma (now dormakaba) is a German maker known for door closers, floor springs and glass door hardware. HCG is sanitary ware and Puyat Steel makes steel products. Source: dormakaba company website.

q: Which brand is known for premium architectural hinges and sliding door systems?
n: Häfele, a German company, supplies premium furniture and architectural hardware, including hinges and sliding door systems. Source: Häfele company website.

q: What hardware goes on a fire exit door?
n: Exit doors in assembly and similar occupancies need panic hardware: a push bar across the door that unlatches when pressed, so a crowd can open it without knowing how. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019, Div. 10 (exits); NFPA 101 Sec. 7.2.1.7.

q: Which door component helps a person in a wheelchair open the door more easily?
n: The kick plate at the bottom of a door takes the push of wheelchair footrests and feet, so a wheelchair user can push the door open without damaging it. Source: BP 344 IRR (doors); ADA Standards Sec. 404 (doors).

q: What is the main disadvantage of using a pivot door in a commercial area?
n: A pivot door turns on top and bottom pivots set in from the edge, which leaves gaps along its edges. It is hard to make airtight, a drawback for air-conditioned commercial spaces. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (pivot doors).

q: Which door type best keeps outside air from entering a building?
n: A revolving door is never open straight through: its wings always seal the drum, so outside air, dust and noise are kept out while people pass. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (infiltration); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which hardware prevents a door from slamming shut?
n: A door damper (hydraulic check) slows the last part of the swing so the door does not slam. A stopper only limits how far it opens. Source: BHMA A156.4 (door controls); manufacturer literature.

q: Which of the following should be considered when ordering doors?
n: The door size (width, height and thickness) is the first item specified when ordering, because jambs, hardware and the opening all follow from it. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; manufacturer ordering guides.

q: What must be known when ordering door jambs?
n: The jamb depth must equal the finished wall thickness so the frame sits flush with both faces of the wall and the casing can cover the joint. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door frames).

q: What sets the height of a door jamb?
n: The jamb height is set by the door leaf height plus clearances at the head and the threshold. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door frames).

q: What sets the clear width between door jambs?
n: The clear width between jambs is set by the door leaf width plus small clearances for swing. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door frames).

q: What is the purpose of a threshold under a door?
o: A seal against air, water, dust and sound
n: A threshold covers the joint where floor finishes meet at a door and seals the gap under the leaf against drafts, water, dust and sound. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (thresholds).

q: Which way must an emergency exit door swing?
o: Outward, in the direction of egress
n: Exit doors must swing in the direction of egress so the flow of escaping people pushes them open rather than jamming them shut. Source: NBC IRR Rule XII Sec. 1207 (exit doors); RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 Div. 10.

q: Which exit door construction gives the best fire resistance?
n: A steel door with a fire-rated core in a labeled rated frame gives the highest fire resistance, up to 3 hours. Wood, hollow-core and glazed doors fail much sooner. Source: NFPA 80, Standard for Fire Doors; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What kind of closer is required on fire-rated exit doors?
n: Fire doors must be self-closing (or close automatically on alarm) so they are shut and keep fire and smoke out of the exit path. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019 (fire doors); NFPA 80.

q: What is added at the bottom of a fire exit door to stop smoke?
n: A smoke seal (gasket or door-bottom sweep) closes the gap around and under a fire door, so smoke cannot leak into the protected stair or corridor. Source: NFPA 105, Smoke Door Assemblies; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What makes a pair of fire exit doors close in the correct order?
n: On a pair of fire doors with an astragal, the coordinator holds the active leaf open until the inactive leaf has closed. That way both latch in the right order and the fire seal is complete. Source: BHMA A156.3; NFPA 80, Standard for Fire Doors.

q: Which of the following is used in sliding windows, providing smooth horizontal movement of glass panels?
n: Figure C shows the rollers for sliding windows, which let the glass panels run smoothly along the track. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.
